hero.subtitle: Why does this matter? Because I learned that the perfect product doesn't exist. Only the one that solves real problems, built by someone who understands design, tech, and business.
hero.supportText: Got an idea you want to turn into a product? A product nobody uses? A team that doesn't get each other? I've been on all three sides of the table. Let's talk.

card.shipDesc: From idea to production in weeks, not months

journey.title: The backwards
journey.subtitle: Most PMs study product management. I took the long route: design, code, and only then product. It was uncomfortable, exhausting, full of mistakes. And that's exactly why I actually know what I'm doing today.

pm.description: Unifying everything I've learned to build things that matter.

achievements.1: -12% payment times (not magic, just fewer useless clicks)
achievements.3: -25% post-release incidents (putting Product, Support, and Engineering in the same room every Friday)

po.description: Bridging business and tech. Translating needs into features.

achievements.1: The real work of Product isn't saying "yes" to everything, but saying "no" to the right things
achievements.2: A beautiful roadmap is useless if it's not aligned with business
achievements.3: User feedback matters more than any internal stakeholder's opinion

dev.description: Writing code. Building APIs. Thinking tech solved everything.

achievements.1: I optimized an algorithm to be 10ms faster while nobody understood how to use the feature
achievements.2: I wrote the most elegant code of my career for a product that died after 4 months
achievements.3: The turning point: "But what's this really for?" - I couldn't answer

designer.description: Designing websites. Managing clients. Thinking I knew everything.

achievements.1: Beautiful design that nobody understands how to use is just art, not product
achievements.2: Perfect mockup that can't be developed is wasted time
achievements.3: The failure: 3 weeks on a design technically impossible within budget

workTogether.title: How we can
workTogether.subtitle: I don't sell consulting. I don't sell hours. I sell results. If you have a concrete problem and want someone who understands design, tech, and business without needing translators, let's talk.

consulting.title: Unlock your product in 90 minutes
consulting.description: Got a product that won't take off? A team going in circles? A roadmap that looks strategic but delivers no results? Let's take 90 minutes.

expectations.dont: Don't expect: Beautiful slides with buzzwords.
expectations.do: Expect: Direct questions, pragmatic analysis, clear action plan.

consulting.idealFor: Ideal for: Founders, Product Managers, Tech Leads who know they're stuck but don't understand where.

brainstorming.title: Two brains, one problem, infinite solutions
brainstorming.description: Sometimes the problem isn't that you don't have solutions. It's that you have too many and don't know which to choose. Or worse, you have the wrong solution to the right problem.
brainstorming.whatWeDo: What we do: Practical work session. Sketches, diagrams, cost-benefit analysis. We leave with solution prototypes, not just vague ideas.
brainstorming.idealFor: Ideal for: Teams in discovery phase, complex architectural decisions, when you need an outsider to challenge your assumptions.

mentorship.title: The path I wish someone had shown me
mentorship.description: Are you a designer wanting to understand development? A developer wanting to move into product? A junior PM wanting to grow?
mentorship.format: Format: 1 hour every 2 weeks. Analysis of your current work. Practical advice. Access to templates and frameworks I use.
mentorship.notForYou: It's not for you if you're looking for someone to tell you what to do. It's for you if you want to learn to think, not just execute.

1.quote: We spent 6 months building features nobody used. One 90-minute session with Mattia and we finally understood what our users actually needed. Three weeks later, we shipped the right thing.
1.author: Sarah Chen

2.quote: My team spoke three different languages: design wanted beauty, engineering wanted clean code, business wanted revenue. Mattia translated all three. Finally, we're building the same product.
2.author: Marco Bianchi

3.quote: I had three architectural solutions and no idea which to choose. Mattia didn't tell me what to do - he asked the questions that made the right answer obvious. That's the difference.
3.author: Alex Kumar

4.quote: As a designer, I always felt like I was guessing what was technically possible. The mentorship gave me the dev perspective I needed. Now I design things that actually get built.
4.author: Elena Rossi
